outline.title: 关于“拜占庭”一词的说明
outline.originalTitle: A Note on the Term Byzantium

en: In modern languages, the term
follows the adjective
with the same ease off the tongue that
follows

But the parallel ends at that superficial level, and the problems begin. For the ancient Athenians really did call themselves Athenians, and they called their state a democracy. When they wanted to refer to their power (or “empire”) over non-Athenians, they called it their hegemony or tyranny. The Byzantines, however, did not call themselves Byzantines and did not call their state an empire. Instead, they consistently called themselves Romans, and they called their state variously the monarchy, polity, power, or public affairs “of the Romans.” They also had a proper name for their state,

(i.e., Romanland), which is absent from most modern discussions. It is debatable which—if any—of these terms might have meant “empire” and in what context. This problem of terminology, moreover, hides a deeper historical one: Does the primary evidence establish whether or to what degree Byzantium actually was an empire? We call it that all the time, but it has never actually been proven or even systematically studied, and here is why.
zh: 在现代语言里，“
”（Byzantine）后接“
”（empire），就像“
”（Athenian）后接“
”（democracy）一样顺口。但两者的相似仅止于此，问题也由此而起。古代雅典人确实自称雅典人，也称自己的国家为民主国。说到他们凌驾于非雅典人之上的权力（或“帝国”），他们称之为自己的霸权或僭主统治。然而，拜占庭人既不自称拜占庭人，也不称自己的国家为帝国。他们一贯自称罗马人，并将自己的国家分别称作“罗马人的”君主国、政治共同体、权力或公共事务。他们还有一个国家专名，
（Romanía，即“罗马之地”），而多数现代讨论都没有提及它。这些术语中是否有哪一个意为“帝国”，又是在何种语境中有此含义，尚可争论。此外，术语问题还掩盖了一个更深的历史问题：第一手史料能否确定拜占庭究竟是不是帝国，又在多大程度上是帝国？我们一直如此称呼它，但这一说法从未真正得到证明，甚至没有经过系统研究。下面就是原因。

en: Let us begin with

In plain English, as well as in many scholarly fields that have recently taken up the topic with vigor, “empire” refers to the domination exercised by one ethnic, ethnoreligious, or ethnopolitical group over a range of others that are perceived as different by the ruling group in the metropole. Empire is not constituted by mere relations of power within a single group, which is a question of political hierarchy and socioeconomic inequality. It focuses specifically on how ethnic differences are reproduced, constituted, or effaced at the level of governance, discourse, and economy. Thus, empire is also not about the form of the regime; that is, about whether it is headed by a monarch who claims the title “emperor.” Republics and democracies also have empires. In fact, the Roman Republic was far more “imperialistic” than the Roman Empire—a paradox that is created by the modern labels “republic” and “empire,” which we use in a way different from the Romans. For the purposes of modern study, the philology of monarchical titles is less important than the history of conquests that are inflected by perceptions of ethnic difference and followed by governance marked by ethnic inequality, regardless of the shape of politics in the metropole.
zh: 先从

说起。在日常英语中，以及近来积极研究这一议题的许多学科中，“帝国”指一个以族群、族群宗教或族群政治为纽带的集团对其他若干集团的支配。帝国中心的统治集团认为后者与自己有别。仅有一个集团内部的权力关系并不构成帝国，那属于政治等级和社会经济不平等的问题。这里专门关注的是族群差异如何在治理、话语和经济层面得到再生产、被建构或被抹去。因此，帝国也不取决于政体形式，即是否由一位自称“皇帝”的君主掌权。共和国和民主国也可以有帝国。事实上，罗马共和国远比罗马帝国更具“帝国主义”色彩。这个悖论源于现代的“共和国”和“帝国”两个称谓，我们的用法与罗马人不同。就现代研究而言，比考辨君主头衔的词义更重要的是考察征服的历史：人们如何看待族群差异，这如何影响征服，而征服之后的治理又如何体现族群不平等。这些问题与帝国中心的政体无关。

en: In other words, empires are by definition

taking a broad view of ethnicity. Byzantium too is often called multiethnic, largely on the grounds that it was an empire. However, both the premise and conclusion are premature. Even though we are now experiencing an “imperial turn” in the study of history, modern theories and definitions of empire have not been systematically applied to Byzantium, where the term is used as if it were self-evident, carried on by the momentum of lingering medieval taxonomies. The Byzantine emperors and their western counterparts famously squabbled over who had the rights to the Roman imperial title, and they quibbled over how exactly their
or

was superior to other kings, earning him the label “emperor” in modern discussions. We can here dispense with this arcane and esoteric philology of titles. Such hoary antiquarian notions buttress conventional terminology and exclude Byzantium from the comparative discussion of empires that is now flourishing.
zh: 换言之，按对族群性的广义理解，帝国就其定义而言是
。拜占庭也常被称为多族群的，主要理由是它是帝国。然而，这个前提和结论都下得太早。尽管历史研究正经历一场“帝国转向”，现代的帝国理论和定义却还没有被系统地用于研究拜占庭。在这个领域，人们仿佛觉得这个词不言自明，沿用至今仍是出于中世纪分类法的惯性。拜占庭皇帝及其西方同行曾为谁有权使用罗马帝号争得不可开交，还争论各自的
或
究竟凭什么高于其他国王，从而在现代论述中获得“皇帝”之称。对于这样艰深冷僻的头衔考辨，这里尽可以搁置。这些陈旧的古物考据观念支撑着习用的术语，却把拜占庭排除在方兴未艾的帝国比较研究之外。

en: A proper study of empire in the case of Byzantium, as the present book aspires to be, requires that we understand who the ruling group was—these “Romans” of Byzantium—and how they were constituted as a group, who the ruled were, and how their relationship was configured within “the polity [etc.] of the Romans.” This, in turn, requires a direct engagement with the problem of ethnicity, which is abundantly attested in the primary sources but rarely (in fact, almost never) discussed in scholarship on Byzantium. Book and article titles that combine
and

are virtually nonexistent. Nor are modern theories of ethnicity used much in them, with the result that in some quarters nineteenth-century notions of fixed “race” still circulate. The study of Byzantium as an empire is, therefore, blocked by the field’s refusal to engage critically and directly with ethnicity.
zh: 要切实研究拜占庭的帝国性质，正如本书所力求做到的，就必须弄清统治集团是谁，也就是拜占庭的这些“罗马人”，他们如何形成一个集团，被统治的是谁，以及他们之间的关系在“罗马人的政治共同体［等等］”中如何安排。这又要求直接面对族群性问题。大量第一手史料都可证明族群性的存在，拜占庭研究却很少讨论这个问题，实际上几乎从未讨论过。几乎没有书或论文的标题同时出现“
”（ethnicity）和“
”（Byzantium）。这些研究也很少使用现代族群理论，以致十九世纪关于固定“种族”的观念在有些地方依然流行。由此，学界拒绝直接而批判地研究族群性，也就阻碍了对拜占庭帝国性质的研究。

en: Why, then, is ethnicity such a problem for Byzantine Studies at a time when it is energetically being discussed and debated in most other disciplines of premodern historical research? The difficulty, in fact, stems not from all the ethnic groups that formed part of Romanía at any given time, but from only

of them, the Romans, who encompassed the majority of the population. Scholars have no difficulty identifying others, who formed larger or smaller minorities, by name (Slavs, Jews, Armenians, Arabs, Franks, foreign mercenaries, and the like). This is justifiable, for they appear in the sources as different from the dominant Roman group and as subject to various policies of assimilation, distinction, or discrimination. However, I note two peculiarities in how these other groups are treated in the scholarship. First, they are usually discussed individually and not as part of a general mapping and articulation of how the nondominant ethnic groups were governed by the ruling one (the Romans). Historians interested in Jews in Byzantium work only on them, and likewise for Armenians, Lombards, and so on. No historian has tried to map all the ethnic groups that existed in the empire. There is much talk of multiethnicity, of the “variety of ethnicities, languages, and religions” that coexisted in the empire, but there is no standard study that backs this talk up with an “ethnic inventory” that weighs the relative presence of each group in the mix.
zh: 既然大多数研究前现代历史的学科都在热烈讨论族群性，为什么这个问题在拜占庭研究中如此棘手？难处其实只在其中

族群，即占人口多数的罗马人，并不涉及每个时期罗曼尼亚境内的所有族群。对于构成大小不等的少数群体的其他人，学者们毫不费力就能说出他们的名字，如斯拉夫人、犹太人、亚美尼亚人、阿拉伯人、法兰克人、外籍雇佣兵等。这是有道理的，因为史料把他们与占主导地位的罗马人区别开来，记载了针对他们的各种同化、区别对待或歧视政策。不过，我注意到，学界研究这些群体时有两个不同寻常之处。第一，学者往往逐一讨论各群体，没有从总体上梳理和阐明占主导地位的罗马人如何治理这些族群。研究拜占庭犹太人的历史学家只研究犹太人，研究亚美尼亚人、伦巴第人的学者也各有各的对象。还没有历史学家试着梳理帝国里曾有过的全部族群。论者一再强调多族群性，强调帝国内并存的“族群、语言和宗教的多样性”，却没有一项公认的研究能用一份“族群清单”支撑这种说法，衡量各群体在其中所占的相对分量。

en: Second, only the minority ethnic groups in Byzantium are recognized by historians, never the majority. This is illogical because the boundary between a minority ethnicity and the majority must, by definition, be an ethnic boundary, meaning that the majority group was also bounded ethnically. If we follow the sources, moreover, we see that the majority clearly defined itself as Roman in a multiplicity of discursive, social, and political sites. Yet in most scholarship this majority remains opaque behind the invented term

This term, in turn, creates fundamental confusions: Does “Byzantine” encompass all subjects of the “Byzantine empire” or only the (otherwise unnamed) majority from whom the (named) minorities were ethnically differentiated? Books vary in their usage. No clarity has emerged, and little effort has been made to seek it. This reticence is strange.
zh: 第二，历史学家只承认拜占庭有少数族群，从不承认多数也是一个族群。这在逻辑上说不通，因为少数族群与多数之间的边界按定义就是族群边界，多数因此也有族群边界。循着史料来看，占多数的人在不同的话语、社会和政治场合都明确地把自己界定为罗马人。然而在大多数学术论述里，这个群体却被“
”这一后造的称谓遮蔽。这个词又引起了根本上的混淆：“拜占庭人”究竟包括“拜占庭帝国”的全体臣民，还是仅指那个未另有名称、在族群上有别于各个具名少数族群的多数？各书用法不一，这个问题一直含混不清，也少有人试图厘清。这样的缄默令人费解。

en: There is a reason behind it, which we need to take by the horns. As an ideological construct in the western imagination, “Byzantium” was shorn of its Roman identity already in medieval times. The dominant conceit in the medieval West was that the majority population of the eastern empire were not Romans as they claimed but rather “Greeks.” This at least recognized that they had an ethnic identity, even if it was mislabeled for political purposes. This tradition of Roman denialism then passed directly from medieval prejudice into modern scholarship, where it continues to fester. In the nineteenth century, moreover, these medieval “Greeks” were stripped of ethnicity and became deracinated “Byzantines.” Roman denialism is today one of the pillars of Byzantine Studies. Whereas visitors from outside the field can easily see that the primary sources speak clearly of a Roman ethnicity, most experts within the field continue to deny the obvious, sometimes zealously, asserting various pretexts, denials, and risible arguments by which to assert that the Byzantines were not “really” the Romans that they claimed to be. In some scenarios, “Roman” was allegedly just an empty label, a relic of past imperial glory or crusty antiquarianism; or it was a hollow piece of political propaganda; or an act of deception performed by a few elites for some reason; or a meaningless claim made by a population that was deluding itself; or it was equivalent to “Orthodoxy”; or any alternative that might avoid the ethnic implications that stare us in the face through so many sources, genres, and contexts, both social and geographical. The modern reading of “Byzantine identity” as religious, and even metaphysical, makes sense only after it had been stripped of its Romanness by self-interested western medieval powers and then stripped of its distorted alter ego, Greek ethnicity, by scholars in the nineteenth century.
zh: 这种缄默背后有个原因，我们必须正面处理。“拜占庭”是西方想象中的意识形态建构，早在中世纪就被剥去了罗马身份。中世纪西方占主流的成见认为，东部帝国的大多数居民并非他们自称的罗马人，而是“希腊人”。这种说法至少承认他们有族群认同，只是出于政治目的安错了名目。这一罗马否认论的传统从中世纪的偏见直接传入现代学术，至今仍在滋长。到了十九世纪，这些中世纪的“希腊人”又被剥去了族群性，成了无根的“拜占庭人”。今天，罗马否认论已成为拜占庭研究的一根支柱。学界外的人一眼就能看出，第一手史料清楚写出了一种罗马族群性，但领域内多数专家依旧否认这件明摆着的事，有时甚至颇为热衷，找出各种借口、托词和可笑的理由，坚持说拜占庭人并非他们自称的“真正的”罗马人。照某些说法，“罗马人”只是个空洞的名号，是帝国昔日荣光或陈腐的好古风气留下的残余，或是一句空洞的政治宣传，或是少数精英出于某种理由施行的欺骗，或是一个自欺的人群提出的无意义主张，或等同于“正教信仰”。总之，什么解释都可以，只要能绕开诸多史料、体裁和社会及地理语境中明摆着的族群含义。只有当“拜占庭认同”先被谋求自身利益的中世纪西方强权剥去罗马性，继而被十九世纪学者剥去作为其歪曲替身的希腊族群性，现代人才可能把它解释为宗教认同，乃至形而上学的认同。

en: As they say in Greece, we have to pull the snake out of this hole. We have to come to terms with the fact that the Byzantines were what they claimed to be, Romans, in ways that were simultaneously (and comprehensively) legal, ethnic, and political. That Romanness is the great taboo, the inconvenient truth, that has held us back in a state of perpetual cognitive dissonance. There is now simply no theoretical justification left for outright denying the ethnicity of a society and imposing upon it an incoherent medley of invented alternatives to accompany the invented label (“Byzantium”) that we have also foisted upon it. Another way of saying this is that we have to align our field with the practice adopted almost universally by the social sciences and humanities during the twentieth century, namely to study identity through the claims and narratives made by the culture in question. Otherwise, we are not understanding who they thought they were and the choices that they made but devising narratives that suit our politics and preconceptions. After we remove this blockage, the path opens for studying ethnicity in Byzantium in a way that is no longer limited to the minorities but can encompass the majority as well. And then we will finally be able to study empire in a rigorous way, because if we cannot ask basic ethnic questions—

children: Who were these self-professed Romans and how did they differ from others?

en: —we cannot answer the basic issue of empire—
Thus, we can properly constitute the study of Byzantium as an empire.
zh: 用希腊人的话来说，我们得把蛇从洞里拖出来。我们必须承认，拜占庭人就是他们自称的罗马人：从法律、族群和政治上看都是如此，而且无不贯彻到底。罗马性便是那项最大的禁忌、令人不快的事实，让我们一直陷在认知失调中。我们已没有任何理论理由可以断然否认一个社会的族群性，为强加给它的杜撰称谓“拜占庭”再配上一堆杜撰而互不相容的解释。换句话说，我们要遵循二十世纪社会科学和人文学科几乎普遍采用的做法，通过所研究的文化自身提出的主张和叙事来研究认同。否则，我们便无法理解他们认为自己是谁、又作了什么选择，只会编造合乎我们自身政治立场和先入之见的叙事。扫除这一障碍之后，我们就能研究拜占庭的族群性，既考察少数，也考察多数。这时我们才能严谨地研究帝国。要是连最基本的族群问题——

children: 这些自称罗马人的人是谁？他们和别人有何不同？

zh: ——都不能提出，就无法回答帝国研究的基本问题——

children: 他们怎样统治非罗马人？

zh: 这样，我们才有可能真正建立起关于拜占庭帝国性质的研究。

en: The plan and argument of the book are as follows. Chapter 1 offers a critique of Roman denialism, from its origins in the late eighth century down to today. Chapters 2 and 3 argue that the Romans of Byzantium were, and knew that they were, an ethnic group. This opens the door, in the second part of the book, to analyze relations between Romans and non-Romans. The case made here for a Roman ethnicity in the middle Byzantine period does not, however, explain how such a thing emerged from the earlier period of Roman rule over Greece and Asia Minor. Roman ethnogenesis in the late antique east must be examined separately, though the argument made here anchors such a study in its end result.
zh: 本书的布局和论点如下。第1章批判罗马否认论，从它在八世纪末的起源说到今天。第2、3章论证拜占庭的罗马人构成一个族群，并且也知道自己就是一个族群。这样，本书第二部就可以进一步分析罗马人与非罗马人的关系。不过，论证中期拜占庭存在罗马族群性，并不能解释它如何从罗马早先对希腊和小亚细亚的统治中形成。晚期古代东部罗马族群的形成须另行考察，本书所做的是为这种考察确定它要解释的结果。

en: Chapter 4 tackles a strategy of imperial rule, namely the acculturation, assimilation, and eventual absorption of foreign groups into the Roman people. This was a way of effectively eliminating foreign ethnicities in the body politic. How were ethnically foreign groups, such as Slavs, Muslims, and Armenians, made into Romans? Chapter 5 examines closely the case of the Armenians in Byzantium, rejecting outdated racial notions that flourish only because “Roman” has been effaced as a viable option. Finally, Chapters 6 and 7 provide an ethnic inventory of the empire at two moments in its history, the early tenth century and mid-eleventh century, respectively. These ascertain whether and to what degree Byzantium was multiethnic and what strategies of distinction shaped its rule over minority populations. As we will see, Byzantium sometimes veered close to being a homogeneous national state, with a vast majority of Romans and small ethnic minorities in the provinces (e.g., in 930 ad), whereas at other times, after a phase of conquests, it veered nearer to being a true empire, the hegemony of Romans over many non-Romans (e.g., by 1050). Sometimes Byzantium was an empire and sometimes not. This requires detailed empirical study for each period using consistent definitions for ethnicity and empire. This book aims to provide both working definitions and empirical evidence.
zh: 第4章讨论帝国统治的一种策略：使外族群体接受罗马文化，再同化并最终将其吸纳为罗马人民的一部分。这是一种消除政治共同体内外来族群差异的有效手段。斯拉夫人、穆斯林和亚美尼亚人等外族群体是怎样成为罗马人的？第5章细察拜占庭境内亚美尼亚人的个案，驳斥陈旧的种族观念。这些观念之所以能流行，只是因为“罗马人”已经被排除在可考虑的身份之外。最后，第6、7章分别列出帝国在十世纪初与十一世纪中叶这两个时期的族群清单，以确定拜占庭是否以及在多大程度上是多族群的，并考察它通过何种区别对待的策略统治少数人口。我们将看到，拜占庭有时接近一个同质的民族国家，罗马人占绝大多数，行省里只有人数不多的少数族群（比如公元930年）；有时经过一轮征服，又接近真正的帝国，即罗马人对众多非罗马人的霸权（比如到1050年）。拜占庭有时是帝国，有时不是。因此，需要以一致的族群性和帝国定义对各个时期作详尽的实证研究。本书旨在给出可供研究使用的定义并提供实证材料。

en: A Note on the Term Byzantium
zh: 关于“拜占庭”一词的说明

en: It is well known that the term

is a modern label for the eastern Roman empire and its people, most of whom called themselves Romans. It is less well known that this term is only the most recent in a series of invented names that the West has devised during the last thousand years precisely in order to avoid using any Roman label in connection with the eastern empire and its people. This book exposes the politics of these invented labels and the historical misunderstandings that result from them. For example, the label “Byzantine” obscures the difference between imperial subjects who were ethnically Roman and those who were not, making it impossible for us to study ethnicity, which in turn makes it impossible to study this state as an empire. Why then, I am often asked, do I still use the term
zh: 众所周知，“

”（Byzantium）是指称东罗马帝国及其人民的现代名称，而其中大多数人自称罗马人。鲜为人知的是，西方在过去一千年里造出了一系列称谓，恰恰是为了避免以任何带有“罗马”的名称来称呼东部帝国及其人民。“拜占庭”不过是其中最晚出现的一个。本书揭示这些后造称谓背后的政治用意及其造成的历史误解。比如，“拜占庭人”这一称谓掩盖了帝国臣民中哪些在族群上是罗马人、哪些不是，从而使我们既无法研究族群性，也就无法把这个国家当作一个帝国来研究。那么，常有人问我，为什么我自己仍使用“
”这个词？

en: The term is still the internationally recognized and conventional name of a specific and still fairly coherent academic discipline: Byzantine Studies. I am a member of that field and address it as such with a contribution to an ongoing debate. Also, we will not solve this problem by making a word taboo. It is better to improve our understanding of the historical reality that lay behind the words that we (fallibly) use. Once we get the substance right, we can then reassess these labels. As noted above, “republic” and “empire” are conventional labels for previous phases of Roman history that were not used that way by the Romans themselves, and this results in more misunderstandings. In the short term, it is possible to retain the label “Byzantium” as a general term for the field and the civilization as a whole, for example in the titles of our books and articles, while referring inside them to Romans and Romanía.
zh: 拜占庭研究是一门范围明确、至今仍相当自成体系的学科，“拜占庭”是国际公认、约定俗成的名称。我是这一学界的一员，希望以研究成果参与领域内仍在进行的争论。此外，把某个词列为禁忌并不能解决问题。我们使用这些词难免出错，更好的办法是加深对它们背后的历史现实的认识。把事实弄清楚之后，我们就可以重新评价这些称谓。如前所述，“共和国”和“帝国”是我们对罗马历史早期阶段的习惯称呼，罗马人自己并不这样使用它们，因而又生出种种误解。短期内，我们可以保留“拜占庭”作为这一学科和整个文明的总称，例如用在书名和论文标题里，同时在正文中用罗马人和罗曼尼亚来称呼那里的人及其国家。
